object_description: compact two-storey volume turned at right angles to the campus around a large atrium
geometry_property: two upper storeys on a base floor
design_condition: the volume is turned at right angles to the existing campus and slightly set back to the east, creating an extended forecourt, while its base floor extends towards the gymnasium and the elementary school

positive: The slight setback of the main building results in an extended forecourt facing the school path
The restriction to two upper storeys helps the building to appear low
The entrance on the western edge of the forecourt intercepts motorised traffic and relieves through traffic
The exit on the second floor with its attractive forecourt links well with the canteen and the rest of the complex
The extension is characterised by an inner hall with surrounding galleries
An open staircase leads from the spacious entrance hall to the upper floors
Corridors have different spatial layering and open to the landscape on both sides
Seminar and teaching clusters with spacious vestibules are proposed on all floors
The art department together with the school kitchen forms a well-designed unit oriented to a south-facing courtyard
The skeleton construction gives a good structure that flexibly covers large and small room requirements in the long term
The static structure is consistently carried down to the parking garage
Floor area, building volume and building costs are in the medium range
A successful contribution that seeks a relationship with the previous buildings through its generous interior space
negative: The generously dimensioned atrium increases the depth of the building and leads to critical proximity to the old gymnasium
The break hall in front and the garage access create an offset from the neighbouring buildings
The traffic solution is too prominent next to the main entrance
The plinth connection to the neighbouring school is too high due to the jump in height
The narrowness towards the gymnasium and the artificial terrain excavation disadvantage the intended outdoor use
The office next to the main entrance and the narrow but long offices and classrooms are not ideally positioned or dimensioned
Docking individual classrooms to the atrium is problematic due to the structural column arrangement
The dark tint of the window sections contrasts too strongly and hard with the in-situ concrete
The heavy window structure suggests a commercial use
The break hall is partially outside the building envelope
The urban setting with the proposed plinth solution and the external expression are not entirely convincing
